questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of write-ahead logging in databases?

options.text: To ensure that all transactions are executed in parallel.
To log changes before they are applied to the database.
To speed up the database recovery process.
To prevent unauthorized access to the database.

questions.explanation: Write-ahead logging ensures that all modifications are logged before they are applied to the database, allowing the system to recover from crashes by using the log to redo or undo transactions.

questions.explanation: Redo operations are used to reapply changes from committed transactions after a crash, ensuring that all committed changes are reflected in the database.
